title: Building a Home Away from Home: ‘Paris Paris’ Explores Displacement, Identity and Belonging
subtitle: Belgian filmmaker Isabelle Tollenaere discusses migration and the universal search for a place to call home, at IFFI 2026
body_text:
Posted On: 27 NOV 2026 1:47PM by PIB Mumbai Release ID: 2342467 Views: 186 A A Print Share X Facebook Instagram WhatsApp Copy Article Link
Read in: English Urdu हिन्दी Nepali Konkani Marathi Gujarati Kannada
Goa, 27 November 2026 Belgian filmmaker Isabelle Tollenaere shared insights into her film Paris Paris , its creative journey and the themes of migration, displacement and belonging at a press conference organised by the Press Information Bureau (PIB) during the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) in Goa today. Featured in the International Cinema category, the film explores the meaning of home through the lives of three men living in the French capital. Set in a building in Paris, Paris Paris follows three men from different backgrounds as they attempt to build a home for themselves in a squatted apartment. Sharing limited resources and exchanging conversations about their past and future, the men navigate questions of identity, displacement and belonging, bringing out the human experiences that connect people across cultures. Expressing her delight at visiting India for the first time, Tollenaere described the opportunity to present her film at IFFI as an honour. She recalled that the screening held the previous day had received an encouraging response, with the auditorium filled to capacity. The engaging question-and-answer session that followed provided an opportunity to interact with Indian audiences and understand their perspectives on the film. Speaking about her creative approach, Tollenaere explained how her background in documentary filmmaking shaped her casting choices. She selected individuals whose personal histories and lived experiences resonated with those of the characters they portray, bringing authenticity and depth to the narrative. The filmmaker also spoke about the challenges involved in the production, particularly those arising from a limited budget and the process of identifying suitable filming locations. Sharing the personal inspiration behind the film, she revealed that her grandparents were immigrants, an experience that shaped her interest in migration, displacement and the search for belonging. Expressing her hopes for the film, Tollenaere said she would love to see it travel across countries and cultures, connecting with audiences around the world through its universal themes and shared human experiences. The press conference was moderated by Andrew Lalchhandama.
